articles.title: Stephen Curry’s rise to NBA’s highest-paid player was about more than three-pointers, as his career choices and endorsement strategy helped build a $203.6 million fortune
articles.summary: Stephen Curry has agreed to a two-year, $116 million extension with the Golden State Warriors, running through the 2028-29 season.
articles.body: Stephen Curry has agreed to a two-year, $116 million extension with the Golden State Warriors, running through the 2028-29 season. The final year is a player option, a route to a 20th season with the same franchise. Curry was eligible for up to $136 million, so the new deal sits about $20 million below the ceiling. Even with the discount, Curry still tops the 2026-27 salary list at $62.6 million. The numbers point to a career built on more than his three-pointers. A run of contracts, a shoe-brand split and a new apparel deal explain how Curry got here.How did Stephen Curry become the NBA’s highest-paid player?Stephen Curry sits first on the 2026-27 contract list at $62.6 million, ahead of Nikola Jokic at $59 million and Jayson Tatum at $58.5 million. Three contracts and one shaky ankle explain most of the climb.Golden State drafted Curry seventh in 2009. Ankle trouble followed, and by 2012 the Warriors had to decide how much to trust the ankle. They offered a four-year, $44 million extension. It became one of the better bargains in league history. Curry won back-to-back MVP awards and the first two of four titles while playing under it.The large numbers arrived next. In July 2017, Curry signed a five-year, $201.2 million deal, the first in NBA history above $200 million. The contract also made Curry the league’s highest-paid player. In August 2021, a four-year, $215 million extension made Curry the first player with two contracts over $200 million. Yearly pay on that one rose from $48.1 million in 2022-23 to $59.6 million in 2025-26. A one-year, $62.6 million extension signed in August 2024 then covered 2026-27.The September deal works differently. Curry was eligible for $136 million and signed for $116 million. Pay drops to $55.7 million in 2027-28 and $60.2 million in 2028-29, with the second year a player option. Golden State general manager Mike Dunleavy said there has never been “a better face to a franchise in professional sports history.”The $62.6 million guard gave the team breathing room too. A smaller number cuts the Warriors’ future payroll commitment, and it fits a long-held plan to finish a career in one uniform. The agreement arrives after a year in which a right knee injury held Curry to 43 games, though he still averaged 26.6 points.How much has Curry earned from contracts and endorsements?Through the 2025-26 season, Curry had collected $470.1 million in NBA salary. Add $62.6 million for 2026-27 and the $116 million extension, and the projected total reaches $648.7 million, provided the final-year option is picked up. Endorsements, investments and other off-court income sit outside that figure.Shoes carry the other big number. Curry began in Nike gear, then signed with Under Armour in 2013. The partnership grew into Curry Brand in 2020, with Curry serving as its president. A 2023 extension was supposed to run past the end of Curry’s playing days. Instead, the relationship ended in November 2025 and Curry Brand went independent. Under Armour kept releasing previously developed Curry products through 2026 while the brand looked at new partners.In June 2026, Curry signed a 10-year agreement with Chinese sportswear company Li-Ning worth more than $400 million, an average of more than $40 million a year. The deal covers signature shoes, basketball apparel, lifestyle products, and golf, with plans for Curry Brand stores in China and the United States. Curry can also sign other athletes under the brand.What else is in Curry’s business portfolio?Beyond sneakers, Curry has endorsement ties with Fanatics, Google, JPMorgan Chase, Panini, Rakuten and 2K Sports. The wider business interests sit under a company called Thirty Ink, covering media, branding, investments and philanthropy.Unanimous Media, co-founded with Erick Peyton in 2018, develops film, television, documentary, publishing and podcast projects with a lean toward sports, family and faith. Curry starred in the 2024 Peacock comedy “Mr. Throwback” and published the photo book “Shot Ready” in 2025. Other ventures include Gentleman’s Cut bourbon and Underrated, a platform that gives overlooked young athletes basketball and golf programs with competition, development and exposure. Estimates put Curry’s net worth at $350 million.What are Curry’s biggest career accomplishments?Curry is a four-time champion, winning in 2015, 2017, 2018 and 2022, and the 2022 Finals MVP. Curry has two MVP awards, and the 2016 vote is the only unanimous one in league history. In 2015-16, Curry averaged 30.1 points, made 402 three-pointers and led Golden State to an NBA-record 73 wins. The same season produced a 50-40-90 shooting year at more than 30 points a game, something no other player has done.The list keeps going. Curry has 12 All-Star selections, 11 All-NBA nods, and two scoring titles, in 2016 and 2021. Eight seasons ended with Curry leading the league in made threes. In March 2025, Curry became the first player to hit 4,000 career threes. Internationally, Curry owns gold from the 2010 and 2014 FIBA World Cups and the 2024 Paris Olympics, where late threes helped beat France in the final.Inside the Warriors’ record book, Curry holds the most All-Star selections (12) and the most All-NBA selections (11) in franchise history.As for Curry’s NBA career, he is one of the greatest to play the sport, with several stunning records and titles to his name. Many argue that Steph should be in the Greatest of All Time (GOAT) debate alongside Chicago Bulls legend Michael Jordan and, of course, LeBron James. Certainly, he deserves the place. Recently, the NBA’s official social media handle posted a short video asking league-wide stars for their opinion on one great NBA skill one would steal. Many called it Curry’s shooting, and some wanted his ball-handling as well. Regardless, Curry is a forged player; he developed into one of the greatest in the game.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Stephen Curry’s projected $203.6M fortune puts LeBron James’ $93.9M earnings in the shade after his $3.9M 76ers decision
articles.summary: Stephen Curry is heading towards a financial milestone that could put him in a league of his own.
articles.body: Stephen Curry is heading towards a financial milestone that could put him in a league of his own. The Golden State Warriors superstar is projected to earn an astonishing $203.6 million over the coming year, creating a huge gap between him and some of basketball's biggest names. LeBron James remains a commercial powerhouse, but his decision to accept a veteran-minimum contract with the Philadelphia 76ers has changed the financial picture. The difference highlights how Curry has turned his success on the court into an enormous business empire.Stephen Curry’s $203.6 million earnings leave LeBron James trailingCurry has secured the top position on Forbes' 2026 list of the NBA's highest-paid players for a second consecutive year. His projected earnings include $62.6 million from basketball and another $141 million from endorsements and business ventures.The off-court figure is particularly striking. It represents a significant increase from the estimated $100 million he generated through commercial activities the previous year.One of the biggest developments behind Curry's growing business portfolio is his partnership with Chinese sportswear company Li-Ning. After ending his relationship with Under Armour in 2025, the Warriors guard agreed to a 10-year deal worth $400 million.The agreement includes a signature footwear collection expected to launch early next year. It gives Curry another major platform to build his brand beyond the NBA.According to Forbes, Curry is the first active NBA player projected to cross $200 million in earnings over a 12-month period. Only Floyd Mayweather, Cristiano Ronaldo and Jon Rahm have previously reached that mark among athletes tracked by the publication.LeBron James’ $3.9 million 76ers contract changes NBA earnings raceJames has slipped to fourth place on the list after spending 11 consecutive seasons at the top of NBA earnings rankings.His projected income stands at $93.9 million, including approximately $90 million from endorsements and business interests. However, his latest contract decision has reduced his basketball earnings considerably.The 76ers signed the veteran superstar to a minimum deal worth approximately $3.9 million. That decision puts his projected total at less than half of Curry's expected earnings.Kevin Durant occupies second place with $104.9 million, while Giannis Antetokounmpo follows at $103.5 million. Anthony Edwards and Jayson Tatum round out the top six with $87.9 million and $86.5 million, respectively.The wider numbers reveal just how valuable NBA stars have become outside basketball. The ten highest-paid players are projected to generate a combined $958 million, with $469 million coming from endorsements and commercial ventures.For Curry, the achievement goes beyond his basketball salary. At 38, he has built a business portfolio that continues to grow even as the competition for NBA earnings intensifies. James remains one of the sport's biggest commercial names, but Curry currently holds the financial advantage.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: NBA rescinds Luka Dončić's technical foul during win over Heat, bringing him back to 1 on the season
articles.summary: Luka Dončić was not happy after receiving the technical foul in the moment on Monday night, and let the officials have it.
articles.body:
Luka Dončić's latest technical foul has been called off.

The league rescinded a technical foul the Los Angeles Lakers star picked up during LA's 138-117 win over the Miami Heat on Monday night. The foul, which Dončić earned in the second quarter at Crypto.com Arena, was reviewed by the league Tuesday.

That has brought Dončić to a single technical foul in eight games this season.

The incident Monday happened after Dončić reacted to a call an official made, which led to a candid conversation between Dončić and the officials on the broadcast.

"I clapped. That's a technical? Come on now," Dončić told the official. "If it was anybody else, you know it's not a technical. Come on now."

Klay Thompson hit the free throw after the technical, which brought the Heat within five points at the time.

Dončić was asked about the technical after the game, but he declined to get into it.

Dončić finished with 42 points, 13 assists and 7 rebounds in the win. He's averaged 43.4 points per game over the last five outings, which included a 52-point night against the Utah Jazz on Oct. 25.

Dončić has had issues with technical fouls. He was suspended for a game last season after reaching the 16-technical foul threshold, which triggers an automatic one-game suspension. He had three straight seasons with 15 technical fouls each, and 13 during the 2024-25 campaign.

Two players in the league already have three technical fouls this season. Golden State star Draymond Green is one of them after he was ejected Monday night for an incident during the Warriors' win over the Phoenix Suns. Houston's Jabari Smith Jr. also has three.

It's still very early in the regular season, and Dončić has a long way to go before having to worry about such a penalty again. But having Monday's rescinded undoubtedly gives him extra room to work with down the stretch.

articles.title: “That would be a giant mistake”: Luka Doncic gets fresh insider warning amid standout season as Los Angeles Lakers’ trade scenario on the horizon
articles.summary: Los Angeles Lakers insider Jovan Buha puts the odds of a trade this season at 65%, and he has a pointed message for the front office.
articles.body: Los Angeles Lakers insider Jovan Buha puts the odds of a trade this season at 65%, and he has a pointed message for the front office. Luka Doncic leads the league in scoring at 38.3 points per game, and the Lakers are 6-2.Buha says sitting still while this is happening would be a costly mistake. Injuries have thinned out the Western Conference, and the roster still has two clear gaps. A deal is unlikely this month. Late December or the February deadline fits better.Is it a mistake for the Lakers to skip a Luka Doncic trade?Buha thinks so. On his podcast, Buha’s Block, he agreed that doing nothing would be malpractice. He then added: “I just think that would be a giant mistake having Luka in his prime.”Luka Doncic is posting the best numbers of his career, and the West is banged up. Anthony Edwards, Chet Holmgren and Cason Wallace are all hurt, which weakens three possible rivals. Slovenian guard is averaging 38.3 points, eight rebounds and 8.1 assists through seven games, shooting 49.7%. Hold that scoring pace all year and it would rank fourth on the NBA’s single-season list. Doncic has already set a handful of franchise and league records, and it has only been two weeks.Buha calls it a window Los Angeles has to use.When could a Lakers trade happen?Probably not soon. Many players who signed this summer cannot be moved until Dec. 15, so Buha sees the last week of December as the earliest realistic point. His best guess is closer to the Feb. 11 deadline.An injury or a bench unit that keeps struggling could speed things up, mostly at center. Walker Kessler is the only true big man on the roster, and nobody reliable sits behind him. The team has also been looking for a starting forward better than the wings it is using now. Buha was careful to say he is not promising anything. He just thinks a deal is more likely than not.There is a contract angle as well. Doncic’s deal runs through 2028 or 2029, depending on his player option. ESPN’s Brian Windhorst said before the season that the Lakers know they need to be in good standing with their star to get an extension done. Giving him a better supporting cast is part of that.Dec. 15 is the date to circle.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ‘I Need to Do Better,’ ‘Maybe I Should Chill’ — Caitlin Clark Makes Honest Admission About Major Source of Criticism
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark has never been shy about showing emotion on the court, but the Indiana Fever star says one part of her competitive reputation may be overstated...
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark has never been shy about showing emotion on the court, but the Indiana Fever star says one part of her competitive reputation may be overstated.

During Tuesday's special episode of Kylie Kelce's "Not Gonna Lie" podcast, she was asked about her on-court behavior, leading to a candid admission about one tendency she knows she needs to work on.

Caitlin Clark Admits Referees Get More of Her Attention Than Opponents

Kelce asked whether the former No. 1 pick was an underrated trash talker, and she disagreed .

"See, people always think that I'm a trash talker. I don't even think I really am," Clark said.

She explained that her exchanges with opponents are usually playful, recalling a moment against Breanna Stewart and the New York Liberty during the 2025 season:

"There was a clip that went viral last year when we played the Liberty and I made a 3 over Stewie. And me and Stewie just both started laughing, 'cause it was funny."

The Fever guard then brought up another part of her on-court behavior:

"I don't really trash talk like that, honestly. I mean, if somebody says something to me, I'll probably go back. Honestly, the people I talk to the most is the refs, which I need to do better at. Maybe I should chill on that a little bit."

Kelce later asked if any particular player stood out as a trash talker. She said opponents rarely direct much trash talk her way.

"People don't really talk trash to me," Clark said, drawing a "What a flex" from Kelce.

The 2024 WNBA Rookie of the Year added that she enjoys those exchanges when they happen.

"I want you to say something to me," Clark said. "And I try to honestly do my best to just act like I can't hear. I love that. I think that's funny."

Her interactions with officials drew attention throughout the 2026 season, including an August technical foul that nearly resulted in a suspension.

During Indiana's 90-86 win over the Chicago Sky on Aug. 8, Natasha Cloud bumped Clark as she drove along the baseline. The Fever floor general passed the ball and went out of bounds, where her momentum carried her into an official.

The contact initially resulted in her eighth technical foul of the season. Fever coach Stephanie White also received one for arguing the call.

Indiana appealed immediately, and the WNBA rescinded the technical, ESPN's Kareem Copeland reported. The decision spared Clark a suspension that would have kept her out of the Fever's Aug. 11 home game against the Liberty.

It was the first time that season the Fever had successfully appealed a technical foul assessed to Clark. Even with the eighth rescinded, her seven technicals were tied for the most in the WNBA at that point.

The three-time All-Star picked up her second technical foul of the playoffs in her final game on Oct. 1. She and Las Vegas Aces forward Brianna Turner were assessed double technical fouls in the first quarter of Game 3 en route to Indiana's season-ending 94-83 road loss.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark’s latest heartwarming gesture sees her send a massive gift to her alma mater
articles.summary: Indiana Fever superstar Caitlin Clark had her former college team, the Iowa Hawkeyes, in mind after the Nike CC1 release. Clark dominated the NCAA with a fou...
articles.body:
Indiana Fever superstar Caitlin Clark had her former college team, the Iowa Hawkeyes, in mind after the Nike CC1 release.

Clark dominated the NCAA with a four-year stint with the Hawkeyes. Although she never won a national championship, losing in the 2023 and 2024 finals, she set countless records for the college and the NCAA as a whole.

Now with her third WNBA season in the rearview, Clark showed love to where she became a national superstar by sending a gift over to the current women's basketball team on the Hawkeyes.

Caitlin Clark gifts CC1s to Iowa Hawkeyes women's basketball team

Clark sent over custom black-and-gold Nike Caitlin 1 signature shoes to the Hawkeyes, creating a player-exclusive Iowa PE colorway for their season-opener against Towson. The team shared a video of the excited reactions current players had to the gift.

The Hawkeyes also shared an in-game picture of how the sneakers looked on the players' feet during the game.

While Clark has previously gifted sneakers to the Hawkeyes team, including pairs of the CC1s, this is the first time she has created a team-exclusive PE for the players, featuring the University of Iowa Tigerhawk logo on the tongue.

The Hawkeyes picked up a convincing 73-45 win over the Towson Tigers in their CBB season-opener on November 3. Junior Dani Carnegie, who was a freshman during Clark's final year with the Hawkeyes, led them to the win with 21 points, five rebounds and five assists.

Clark left the Hawkeyes without a championship, but set the NCAA Division 1 basketball scoring record with 2,951 points, breaking Pete Maravich's 54-year-old 3,667-point record.

She has also made the most three-pointers in NCAA history with 548, with her 201 threes in 23-24 setting the record for most in one season.

Her legacy as a Hawkeye is arguably richer than any current professional athlete due to the historic nature of her four-year tenure. While not having a championship to cement it as the greatest NCAA career of all time is rough, she gave Iowa years of incredible basketball.

articles.title: ‘This Would Literally Ruin Basketball,’ ‘Do Not Do That’ — NBA World Outraged As Adam Silver ‘Likes the Idea’ Of 40-Minute Games
articles.summary: NBA fans are pushing back against the possibility of shorter games after a recent report suggested Adam Silver prefers reducing NBA contests from 48 to 40 mi...
articles.body:
NBA fans are pushing back against the possibility of shorter games after a recent report suggested Adam Silver prefers reducing NBA contests from 48 to 40 minutes.

Sports Illustrated's Chris Mannix recently discussed the commissioner's preference, but the idea is not new, and Silver has openly supported it before.

NBA Fans Outraged as Adam Silver's 40-Minute Game Preference Resurfaces

Mannix discussed the possibility during a recent appearance alongside Rachel Nichols on Sports Illustrated. He said Silver likes the idea of replacing the NBA's traditional four 12-minute quarters with four 10-minute periods, bringing games in line with the international format.

"Adam Silver likes the idea of 40-minute games. Adam's a globalist when it comes to basketball. But I just don't see financially how it is feasible," Mannix said .

He also explained that shortening games would not necessarily reduce the workload of the biggest stars. Instead, he believes players further down the rotation would lose opportunities.

The comments quickly drew criticism from basketball fans, many of whom believe changing the length of NBA games would affect the sport's identity and history.

"This would literally ruin basketball," one hoops fan wrote .

A Pacers fan account also warned about the impact on historical comparisons, saying : "NO… this would change basketball history and how we compare stats across generations."

Others directed their frustration at the commissioner, as one user wrote : "Adam Silver needs to be fired IMMEDIATELY."

"This dude sucks at his job," a sports content creator quipped.

However, the first time Silver publicly expressed the idea was in January 2025. He appeared on The Dan Patrick Show and openly said he was a fan of four 10-minute quarters.

"As we get more involved in global basketball, the NBA is the only league that plays 48 minutes," Silver explained . "I am a fan of four 10-minute quarters."

Silver argued that a two-hour game would better fit modern television viewing habits, citing Olympic and college basketball, both of which use a 40-minute format. He also acknowledged that shortening games could affect records and statistics, although he said he was putting those concerns aside when discussing the idea.

At the time, ESPN reported that NBA games averaged 2 hours and 16 minutes, making them considerably longer than the two-hour format Silver preferred. The discussion also drew opposition from coaches.

A switch would have significant consequences beyond the length of games. NBA games have featured four 12-minute quarters throughout the league's history, and reducing them to 10 minutes would make many scoring and playing-time records harder to compare across generations.

While Mannix's latest comments have revived an old debate, they do not mean the league is preparing to introduce 40-minute games.

articles.summary: Campazzo, Maledon y Jantunen se unen a Deck y Garuba en una enfermería blanca saturada. Nunn, Sloukas y Francisco, tridente exterior griego, gran amenaza
articles.body: El Real Madrid recibe al Panathinaikos en uno de los grandes clásicos del baloncesto continental, dos equipos que están en todas las quinielas para estar en la Final Four de Abi Dabi (28 y 30 de mayo) con la que sueñan para ampliar su formidable botín de la máxima competición: Nadie tiene más Copas de Europa que los blancos (11), seguidos por el CSKA (8) y por los atenienses (7). Son grandes entre los grandes, como lo es también Zeljko Obradovic, el entrenador más laureado de Europa con nueve coronas, cuatro de ellas conquistadas con el Panathnaikos, que ha recuperado para el banquillo a su ídolo en un intento por rememorar su época gloriosa bajo su batuta (campeones en 2000, 2002, 2007, 2009 y 2011) tras haber ganado un sólo entorchado (2024) en las últimas 15 temporadas. Para poder conseguirlo, o al menos intentarlo, además de rescatar a Zeljko Obradovic del baúl de los recuerdos, ha tirado la casa por la ventana para reforzar a un equipo plagado de jugadores top. Dimitris Giannakopoulos, su excéntrico dueño, que ya tenía en nómina a Nigel Hayes-Davis, Kendrick Nunn, Mathias Lessort, Juancho Hernangómez, Konstantinos Mitoglou, Jerian Grant o Kostas Sloukas, ha fichado a Sylvain Francisco, Brancou Badio, Guerschon Yabusele, Isaac Bonga, Moustapha Fall y Lefteris Mantzoukas. Órdago a grandes. El Real Madrid-Panathinaikos sería uno de los mejores partidos que se pueden ver hoy en día en Europa de no ser porque los blancos, tras alcanzar la velocidad de crucero en su juego con 11 victorias seguidas, seis en la Euroliga (Partizan, Armani, ASVEL, Maccabi, Baskonia y Fenerbahce) y cinco en la Liga Endesa (Obradoiro, Manresa, Bilbao, Lleida y Burgos), pueden perder fuelle por culpa de la brutal plaga de lesiones que ya padecían y se ha recrudecido en la última semana. Usman Garuba, con rotura del tendón de Aquiles de su pierna derecha y que ni siquiera ha debutado, y Gaby Deck, operado por una inestabilidad anterior en el hombro izquierdo, fueron los primeros en caer con lesiones graves. Y la semana pasada la enfermería blanca continuó llenándose con las bajas de Mikael Jantunen (rotura completa de la fascia plantar del pie izquierdo), Théo Maledon (esguince de rodilla derecha) y Facundo Campazzo, que el domingo sufrió una lesión muscular en el partido de Liga ante el Burgos. Y suerte para los blancos que Nick Smith Jr (fascitis plantar leve), podrá reaparecer, aunque no a tope porque le falta ritmo. El panorama es preocupante para Pedro Martínez, que con tanta baja se ve obligado a recurrir a jugadores con los que prácticamente no contaba habitualmente, como Max Shulga, Alex Sarr o Sergio Llull, con un solo partido jugado de los dos primeros en la Euroliga y ninguno del menorquín. Los tres sí tuvieron más minutos y protagonismo del habitual el domingo ante el San Pablo Burgos, con actuaciones más que aceptables. Pero el equipo de Porfirio Fisac, con todos los respetos que merece, no aglutina ni de lejos tantas amenaza como el de Zeljko Obradovic. Ni sus bases constituyen una amenaza tan descomunal como la que ejercen Kendrick Nunn, Kostas Sloukas o Sylvain Francisco. Tras manejadores de primerísimo nivel que con las bajas seguras de Maledon y de Campazzo tendrían que ser contenidos por Feliz, Smith Jr., Llull e incluso Shulga. Pedro Martínez admite que tanta baja le ha obligado a cambiar su plan de juego: "Entrenar, entrenamos igual. Nuestra identidad y nuestros valores nos gustaría que fueran los mismos. Pero sí que es verdad que nos tenemos que adaptar un poco. Seguramente no vamos a poder jugar durante muchos minutos con un base puro porque no los tenemos. Vamos a tener que jugar algo diferente. Lo hemos hablado hoy para intentar adaptarnos a la situación que tenemos, pero ojalá que las bajas no nos quiten la forma en la que queremos jugar", explicó. Quien no se fía del Madrid ni baja la guardia por las ausencias de los blancos es Zeljko Obradovic: "Conozco las noticias sobre Campazzo y Maledon, pero tienen suficiente calidad en su plantilla para jugar bien y cubrir las ausencias. Son dos jugadores muy importantes, pero su equipo tiene recursos suficientes para competir y jugar un buen baloncesto incluso sin ellos", aseguró el entrenador del Panathinaikos, que tiene clara la clave del partido: "El Real Madrid juega rápido y nosotros también tenemos que jugar bien para frenar su ritmo. Tenemos que controlar nuestro ataque, no permitirles correr y limitar nuestras pérdidas de balón".

articles.title: Rwanda's army team removed from BAL after US sanctions, NBA says
articles.summary: The US imposed sanctions on Rwanda's army over its role in the conflict in DR Congo.
articles.body:
The National Basketball Association (NBA) says it removed Rwanda's army team from its African league because of US sanctions imposed on the country in March.

The NBA had previously said the Rwandan army-funded Armée Patriotique Rwandaise (APR) club would not participate in the 2026 Basketball Africa League (BAL).

However this is the first time the NBA has revealed the reasons behind the APR's removal.

The association was responding to complaints by two US senators, who sent a letter asking them to reconsider their partnership with the Rwandan team. The US placed sanctions on the Rwandan army, accusing it of fuelling the conflict in the Democratic Republic of Congo in March.

The senators said the NBA risked "becoming complicit in sportswashing by accepting money from a Rwandan government that systematically abuses human rights".

Last week, the US also imposed sanctions on Rwanda's defence ministry over its support for the M23 rebel group which has seized control of large parts of eastern DR Congo. Rwanda denies backing the rebels despite overwhelming evidence.

Rwanda is an official BAL partner and pays the league to host its finals at the 10,000-seat BK Arena in the capital, Kigali.

The evidence that shows Rwanda is backing rebels in DR Congo

In the letter to the NBA dated 23 October, Democratic Senator Jeffrey Merkley and Republican counterpart Marsha Blackburn gave the association until 2 November to give a written response regarding its continued partnership with Rwanda.

"What is the NBA red line for accepting money from foreign governments that commit human rights abuses?" the senators asked.

Among other queries, they also questioned how the association could "reconcile its continued partnership with Rwanda with its purported commitment to justice".

In its response, NBA deputy commissioner Mark Tatum said the Rwandan team "had been withdrawn" from the BAL following the sanctions imposed earlier in the year, American sports website ESPN reports.

The NBA said the APR basketball club would remain barred while the US sanctions are in place.

The APR is one of Rwanda's top basketball teams and represented the country in the BAL in 2024 and 2025, when it came third. It was replaced by the RSSB Tigers this year.

The BAL is a pan-African basketball league established and co-organised by the NBA and the basketball's world governing body Fiba.

It is a professional league featuring 12 club teams from across the continent.

Rwanda has hosted all but one of the league's final and playoff matches since the inaugural match in 2021.

The NBA reportedly receives millions of dollars annually from the country for the marketing and partnership rights.

DR Congo has repeatedly condemned Rwanda's high-profile international sports deals, including with the NBA, European football clubs and Formula 1, asking them to end their campaigns.

It argues that these help Rwanda clean up its global image, while the conflict continues in eastern DR Congo.

articles.title: Los Angeles Lakers Trade Idea to Land a New Dream Target
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers (6-2) have gotten off to a strong start to the 2026-27 season, but clear weaknesses remain.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers (6-2) have gotten off to a strong start to the 2026-27 season, but clear weaknesses remain.

Behind starting center Walker Kessler, the team has questionable depth, with Jarred Vanderbilt recently displacing Kevon Looney as head coach JJ Redick's primary backup. Sandro Mamukelashvili fills a need as an offensive option, but the Lakers aren't exactly deep at his natural power forward position.

Before the season began, B/R ranked L.A.'s top trade targets , mainly to add needed size to the roster.

A recent disagreement between Charlotte Hornets head coach Charles Lee and big man Naz Reid should pique the Lakers' interest.

Trade season doesn't really kick in until Dec. 15 and runs through the Feb. 11 deadline. If Reid and the Hornets consistently aren't on the same page, add him to the Lakers' wish list.

The Los Angeles Lakers receive: Naz Reid, Tidjane Salaün

The Charlotte Hornets receive: Cameron Carr, Adou Thiero, Jarred Vanderbilt, Jaden Hardy, $23.3 million trade exception (Naz Reid), 2032 first-round pick swap, 2033 second-round pick

The Lakers' biggest acquisition this offseason was the Walker Kessler sign-and-trade, which sent nearly all their remaining future draft compensation to the Utah Jazz to make the deal.

The front office built around the Luka Dončić-Austin Reaves-Kessler trio as well as it could, but the Lakers' lack of bench depth has already been exposed. If the Hornets were willing to take L.A.'s package for Reid, the Lakers would jump at the opportunity—even giving up two young prospects they value highly in Carr and Thiero.

Reid would presumably start at power forward, then rotate to center when Kessler sits. The Lakers don't improve defensively, but they add high-end depth, and Reid is a significant offensive upgrade. Vanderbilt has played a role in recent games with Ziaire Williams nursing a foot injury but hadn't been a rotation staple during Redick's reign.

Salaün, in his third season, has yet to pop. The Hornets declined his fourth-year $10.4 million option, making him an unrestricted free agent in July 2027.

The trade would need to wait until close to the deadline to allow the Lakers to return to the required 14 players. Los Angeles would acquire Reid via the expanded traded player exception of Vanderbilt and Hardy; Salaün works similarly for Carr and Thiero. The timing to replenish the roster would be simpler if they found a taker for Looney (or Bronny James) without salary coming back. If so, L.A. could sign three prorated minimum players (to the maximum 15) while staying below its $209 million first-apron hard cap.

At this early stage of the season, the Hornets wouldn't seriously consider this Lakers offer.

L.A. would need the disconnect between Lee and Reid to become untenable. Reid was benched for the second half of Charlotte's 97-89 loss to the Detroit Pistons on Oct. 28.

"Unfortunately, Naz didn't meet our standards in the first half and at halftime we made the decision that he wouldn't play in the second half," Lee told reporters after the game . "But I look forward to him meeting those standards come next game."

Should Reid, who is owed $80.2 million over the next three years (player option before final season), become a liability for the Hornets, the Lakers would still need to have the best offer.

Given L.A.'s lack of first-round picks and the early-season injuries to Carr and Thiero, Los Angeles would need the market for Reid to be soft. Carr, the No. 24 pick in the June draft, was a summer-league standout who played respectably through the preseason. Similarly, Thiero has significant potential but has struggled to stay healthy.

The Lakers would need to showcase the pair successfully to build their value before Charlotte even considered a deal. The Hornets would try to get the Lakers to include their two future second-rounders via the Washington Wizards (2031 and 2032), which shouldn't be a deal-breaker for L.A.

Charlotte has already tipped its hand on Salaün by declining his option. Roster space remains an issue. The Hornets would either need to cut two players (presumably one would be Liam McNeely) before the deal with the Lakers or rope in a third team to take in McNeely and Hardy.

The Hornets would take Vanderbilt for Salaün, absorbing the other incoming Lakers into preexisting trade exceptions (Collin Sexton, Dorian Finney-Smith, and Mason Plumlee). This allows the team to generate the large exception for Reid.

Add Reid to the Lakers' list, but for the Hornets, it's a deal they make only right before the deadline, in the absence of better offers, assuming Reid proves to be miscast on the team's roster.

articles.title: 2027 WNBA Free Agent Big Board Features Star Power in Napheesa Collier, Kelsey Plum, More
articles.summary: A historic 2026 WNBA season has come to a close, with the Golden State Valkyries winning the title in just their second year as a franchise. A recent expansion team achieving this feat reflects the explosion of talent in today's game; it's an exciting time for the league, and the first year of the new collective bargaining agreement has to be considered a massive success for all involved.
articles.body:
A historic 2026 WNBA season has come to a close, with the Golden State Valkyries winning the title in just their second year as a franchise. A recent expansion team achieving this feat reflects the explosion of talent in today's game; it's an exciting time for the league, and the first year of the new collective bargaining agreement has to be considered a massive success for all involved.

With 2026 in the rearview mirror and the draft months away, WNBA teams will soon begin their offseason by looking at free agency to shore up their rosters. Though the 2027 class isn't as stacked as 2026's historic group (when almost every veteran in the league was an unrestricted free agent), plenty of franchise-changing players are still available.

There are four bona fide, All-WNBA-caliber players on the market. Behind them are a handful of restricted free agents who could be on the cusp of stardom. Of course, several impactful role players round out this crop; the most savvy teams will find value there.

Taking all of this into consideration, let's look at the 10 best free agents on the board, what makes them special, and where they might end up.

After an uneven start to her career in Indiana and Dallas, Smith found her footing in Vegas next to A'ja Wilson. The 6'4 " forward and former No. 2 overall pick fit like a glove in Becky Hammon's system, helping the Aces win the title in 2025.

Before her Aces stint, Smith struggled with shot selection, efficiency, and defensive effort. Those areas have all improved dramatically in Vegas. That's allowed Smith's imposing physicality and rebounding prowess to shine. Last season, Smith put it all together and became one of the most impactful power forwards in the WNBA.

Unfortunately, Smith suffered a season-ending knee injury in August (likely an ACL tear). This couldn't have come at a worse time, as Smith was set to cash in for a potentially large payday in unrestricted free agency. Even with the injury, Smith should be a hot commodity in a relatively weak market. Playing alongside A'ja Wilson is a situation Smith might not want to leave, but plenty of teams could benefit from her services.

Thornton is one of the most steady veterans in the league. She took her game to a new level in Golden State. The 34-year-old wing made the All-Star team in 2025, the first selection of her career. Sadly, she underwent knee surgery shortly after, ending her season prematurely. Despite taking a step back in 2026, Thornton still has plenty of winning attributes that contending teams covet.

Though often billed as a classic three-and-D wing, Thornton is a streaky shooter (career 32.4% from three). But she takes and makes enough to provide some spacing while affecting the game in other ways. Thornton is a smart cutter and off-ball mover. She can leverage her strength to attack closeouts.

Most of Thornton's value comes on the other end, where she's long been one of the better wing defenders in the league. Thornton doesn't generate a ton of steals or blocks, but she's a strong individual and team defender you can trust to guard up and down the lineup. Any contending team needs a Kayla Thornton, and if she gets squeezed out of Golden State's plans, there will be plenty of other offers available. Dallas, Indiana, and Vegas are all playoff hopefuls who could be good fits.

Another Valkyries wing hits the free-agent market, albeit in restricted status. It's hard to imagine Golden State letting Thornton or Zandalasini walk, but it's possible a team throws a big enough bag to force the issue.

Zandalasini would likely be the more coveted player, despite her restricted status. She is one of the best wing shooters in the league (her uncharacteristic 32% mark from three in 2026 can be entirely dismissed) and does some fun things with the ball in her hands at 6'2".

Zandalasini has improved defensively, too. Over the last two years in Golden State, the Valkyries have posted a 99.0 defensive rating with Zandalasini on the floor, compared to a 101.6 mark with her off.

Again, with Zandalasini restricted, Golden State will most likely bring her back. But she is due for a large pay raise. With Gabby Williams, Janelle Salaun, Kaila Charles, and Kayla Thornton all on the wing, Golden State might not be willing to pay up. If Zandalasini leaves, she'd fit on almost any team that can afford her.

Dream Unrivaled Trios We'd Like to See 🤩

Burrell had a career season in 2026 and became one of the Sparks' most important players. The 6'2 wing averaged a career-high 14.2 points and doubled her three-point volume, shooting 38% on more than four attempts per game. Burrell is a special athlete with great burst and quickness. She has a rare combination of skills for her size, especially given her shooting improvement.

Burrell's next step is to make more of an impact on defense. For someone with her athletic tools, she isn't very good on that end; her modest steal and block totals (1.4 combined last season) reflect this. Burrell often gets lost off-ball, too, which is indicative of another issue with her game: poor feel.

Even with the issues, Burrell is a very good player who took a meaningful step forward last season. The Sparks would probably like to keep her around, but if someone throws a big offer sheet her way, it might not be worth matching. Teams like New York, Chicago, and Houston come to mind as potential suitors.

Engstler was one of many Fire players to enjoy a breakout season in 2026, averaging career highs in every statistical category. Fire coach Alex Sarama seemed to unlock the potential that Engstler always had, turning her into a two-way force.

Seriously, few players can give you 10 points and six rebounds, shoot 37% from three on solid volume, and add 2.8 steals + blocks per game. Engstler was the ultimate Swiss Army knife in 2026 and is entering restricted free agency, due for a large pay bump.

Based on Engstler's comments, staying in Portland seems most likely. The Fire also has the most cap space in the league, so retaining her shouldn't be an issue, even if she commands a large offer sheet from rival teams. But those teams should absolutely force Portland to pay up, because Engstler is a winning player who seems to have found herself in year five.

Perhaps no WNBA player raised her free-agent stock in 2026 more than Awak Kuier. Originally drafted second overall as a raw 19-year-old in 2021, Kuier struggled mightily in the league for her first three seasons. She took 2024 and 2025 off, playing full-time in Europe and developing in a context that gave her more opportunities to grow.

Kuier returned last season and became a crucial component of the Wings' historic turnaround. Coach Jose Fernandez demanded a lot from Kuier and was sporadic with her minutes, but that tough love paid off in the long run; Kuier ended the season on a tear, averaging 3.7 blocks per game over the Wings' final 10 contests.

It's impossible to overstate Kuier's impact on the Wings' defense. Prior to 2026, Dallas had never even been a league-average defensive team. Kuier helped change that. The Wings posted a stingy 102.9 defensive rating in her minutes. The physical tools Kuier possesses are nuts. Her 6'6 frame is complemented by a massive wingspan and impressive lateral quickness.

Kuier also made strides offensively; she became a reliable spot-up shooter from three, improved as a decision-maker off the roll, and flashed some intriguing creation ability. It feels like Kuier's been around forever, but she's still just 25 years old. With that in mind, she'll draw near-max offers from suitors in restricted free agency. It would be insane for Dallas to let her go, but teams like Portland, Golden State, and Toronto could try to pry her away.

Plum represents a tier shift in this year's free agent class. The top four free agents are all perennial All-WNBA candidates. They are all unrestricted. Plum kicks that group off, as she's in an interesting spot in her career.

The Mercury, far out of the playoff picture at the time, shocked the world by trading for Plum at the deadline last season. They gave up a valuable 2027 first-round pick and promising guard Monique Akoa Makani in the deal, which is a steep price to pay for an impending unrestricted free agent. Phoenix hoped Plum would help them make a late-season run and sneak into the playoffs, igniting a run toward a long-shot championship.

It didn't work out that way. Now, the Mercury has to re-sign Plum to avoid a complete disaster. Funny enough, a big reason Phoenix missed the playoffs was that Plum played just five games after the trade because of an injury. Though Plum has been mostly healthy over the last few seasons, she did tear her Achilles in 2020. It's fair to wonder how much longer the 32-year-old guard can perform at an elite level, especially since she relies a lot on burst and quickness to get downhill.

Still, Phoenix can't afford to let Plum walk. Even with her age and injury concerns, she'll likely command a long-term max deal. The biggest threat to Phoenix would likely be the Valkyries, who could use an offensive engine to make life easier.

Fresh off her second straight All-WNBA First Team selection, Mitchell enters unrestricted free agency for the first time. If we're reading the tea leaves, it seems very possible that Mitchell could be on the move. Comments from her exit interview hinted at possible exasperation with the chaotic environment surrounding the Fever, so it wouldn't be shocking to see Mitchell sign elsewhere.

Whoever lands Mitchell is getting one of the greatest offensive players in the game's history. In 2026, Mitchell put up the most efficient scoring season ever, averaging a staggering 24.7 points per game on 64% true shooting. Her combination of speed and shooting touch is unmatched. Mitchell is still at the peak of her powers.

There's no doubt Mitchell has greatly benefited from Caitlin Clark's gravity and playmaking over the last few years. At the same time, she's proven over and over again that she can perform at a similar level without Clark on the floor. While Mitchell's defense leaves a lot to be desired, it's hard to find a more complete offensive player in this league. Wherever Mitchell goes, she'll demand a long-term max deal. Mitchell fits on every team, but it would be cool to see her go somewhere like Seattle or Los Angeles and help a rebuilding team take the next step.

Young gets the nod over Mitchell on this list for being two years younger and offering far more defensive utility. The 6'0 wing is coming off a typical Jackie Young season, stuffing the stat sheet and earning All-WNBA Second Team honors.

It's remarkable how Young has consistently improved throughout her career. She's gone from a complete non-shooter to a genuine threat from three. In 2026, she took another playmaking leap. Young averaged a career-high 6.8 assists per game (2.4 turnovers), fourth in the league. This is a complete player who does everything on both ends of the floor at the prime of her career.

Young has enjoyed an enormous amount of success in Vegas as the Robin to A'ja Wilson's Batman, winning three titles. Here's the big question: does Young want to step out from behind Wilson's shadow? Does she want to prove that she can be the alpha, 1A player on her own team? Do those kinds of narratives matter to her at all?

If the answer to those questions is "yes" and Young entertained leaving Vegas, she would certainly be able to pick her next destination. Whichever team she wants to go to would move heaven and Earth to add her.

Make no mistake about it– Napheesa Collier is the top free agent of the 2027 class. Though her 2026 season was marred by injury and playoff failure, Collier is still one of the best three players in the league. It's easy to forget that just a year ago, Collier had a legitimate MVP case against prime A'ja Wilson.

When healthy, Collier is likely the best (non-Wilson) two-way player in the WNBA. Collier won Defensive Player of the Year in 2024 and has made five All-Defense teams. Though 2026 was considered a "down" year, Collier flirted with a 50/40/90 shooting season while scoring 17 points per game. You can pretty much bet that Collier is good for a 21/8/3 line with elite defense for the next handful of years.

Collier raised eyebrows last season when she opted for a one-year, supermax contract to return to Minnesota instead of agreeing to a long-term deal. After how last season ended, it wouldn't be surprising to see the Lynx move on and go all in on Olivia Miles.

While Collier and Miles are certainly talented enough to figure things out together, their playstyles are a bit incongruous. Miles wants to run a heavy amount of spread pick-and-roll, while Collier prefers a more methodical attack, working from the elbows and letting the offense flow from there. It just seems like both parties may decide it's best to go their separate ways. If that happens, Dallas, New York, and Phoenix could all be compelling fits.
